name: BuntDB
tagline: Embeddable in-memory key/value store for Go with ACID transactions, custom and spatial indexes, and TTLs.
description: BuntDB is a pure-Go, in-process key/value store by Josh Baker (tidwall) that keeps the whole dataset in memory and persists it to a durable append-only file that it compacts in the background. What sets it apart from a map or bbolt is indexing: you can declare B-tree indexes over values with custom comparators, index fields inside JSON values, build multi-value indexes, and create R-tree spatial indexes over up to 20 dimensions, then iterate ranges or nearby items inside read-only or read/write transactions with rollback. Keys can carry TTLs for cache-style eviction. It is mature and essentially feature-complete: v1.3.2 shipped in September 2024 and later commits are documentation only. Use it when the data fits in RAM and you want indexes without running a server.
statusNote: Feature-complete; last code release v1.3.2 (Sept 2024), with only documentation commits since.

scale.notes: Whole dataset must fit in RAM; persistence is a single append-only file rewritten in the background.

strengths: Secondary B-tree indexes with custom comparators, including indexes on JSON fields
R-tree spatial indexes over up to 20 dimensions for intersects and nearby queries
Read/write transactions with rollback on a single-writer, multi-reader lock
Per-key TTL expiry and a durable append-only file with configurable fsync
Pure Go with no cgo, so it embeds trivially
weaknesses: Entire dataset lives in memory, so capacity is bounded by RAM
Only one writer at a time limits write concurrency
No replication or network server; you build that yourself
useCases: Embedded state or config store inside Go services
Indexed data access in prototypes without a database server
